source_manifestation.description: Nihonium is the emergent stability of 113 Protons and 113 Electrons with 173 Neutrons, bound by Electromagnetic and Strong Nuclear Forces.

0dac2fc5a4921c6e4aa7c677705a1773fdae76f1.name: Element: Flerovium (Fl)
0dac2fc5a4921c6e4aa7c677705a1773fdae76f1.language: Flerovium (Z=114). A Solid (Phase 3) with Other/Unknown potential. Valence 4. Tension: 5. A Post Transition element in period 7.

source_manifestation.description: Flerovium is the emergent stability of 114 Protons and 114 Electrons with 175 Neutrons, bound by Electromagnetic and Strong Nuclear Forces.

6c33074defdd27f43741816d4f21aaedcc968ba7.name: Element: Moscovium (Mc)
6c33074defdd27f43741816d4f21aaedcc968ba7.language: Moscovium (Z=115). A Solid (Phase 3) with Other/Unknown potential. Valence 5. Tension: 7. A Post Transition element in period 7.

source_manifestation.description: Moscovium is the emergent stability of 115 Protons and 115 Electrons with 175 Neutrons, bound by Electromagnetic and Strong Nuclear Forces.

c48caa651a87c115de58ab7392fa84e1a71cab64.name: Element: Livermorium (Lv)
c48caa651a87c115de58ab7392fa84e1a71cab64.language: Livermorium (Z=116). A Solid (Phase 3) with Other/Unknown potential. Valence 6. Tension: 5. A Post Transition element in period 7.

source_manifestation.description: Livermorium is the emergent stability of 116 Protons and 116 Electrons with 177 Neutrons, bound by Electromagnetic and Strong Nuclear Forces.

a89f893a2dafa7818cc403397474e2ef0ee16c03.name: Element: Tennessine (Ts)
a89f893a2dafa7818cc403397474e2ef0ee16c03.language: Tennessine (Z=117). A Solid (Phase 3) with Other/Unknown potential. Valence 7. Tension: 6. A Halogen element in period 7.

source_manifestation.description: Tennessine is the emergent stability of 117 Protons and 117 Electrons with 177 Neutrons, bound by Electromagnetic and Strong Nuclear Forces.

b081b254bdc40753ef644a59e5c3757197022910.name: Element: Oganesson (Og)
b081b254bdc40753ef644a59e5c3757197022910.language: Oganesson (Z=118). A Gas (Phase 1) with Other/Unknown potential. Valence 8. Tension: 7. A noble gas closure at period 7, full shell stability.

source_manifestation.description: Oganesson is the emergent stability of 118 Protons and 118 Electrons with 176 Neutrons, bound by Electromagnetic and Strong Nuclear Forces.

1d22f4f14e315b02f7eec820bcde444bfb5a7f7c.name: Entropy
1d22f4f14e315b02f7eec820bcde444bfb5a7f7c.language: Entropy is the measure of disorder or randomness in a system. In thermodynamics, it quantifies the unavailability of thermal energy for conversion to mechanical work. In information theory, it measures the average information content or uncertainty in a message.
1d22f4f14e315b02f7eec820bcde444bfb5a7f7c.script: entropy = -sum(p * math.log(p) for p in probabilities if p > 0)

b9114fdb55ba2553168d3fee8f7fdb6f54efe13a.name: Symmetry
b9114fdb55ba2553168d3fee8f7fdb6f54efe13a.language: Symmetry is the property of an object or system remaining unchanged under a set of transformations. Physical laws exhibit symmetries that correspond to conservation laws via Noether's theorem. Symmetry breaking leads to phase transitions and emergent phenomena.
b9114fdb55ba2553168d3fee8f7fdb6f54efe13a.script: is_symmetric = all(transform(x) == x for transform in transformations)

bda54d6e38231f11daf2b3d772533e6a2ac28ead.name: Resonance
bda54d6e38231f11daf2b3d772533e6a2ac28ead.language: Resonance occurs when a system oscillates at maximum amplitude at specific frequencies. The resonant frequency depends on the system's physical properties. Energy transfer is most efficient at resonance, enabling phenomena from musical instruments to quantum tunneling.

c9f5cf94dd521a4d211c7a7dc353c7615c0284cc.name: Coherence
c9f5cf94dd521a4d211c7a7dc353c7615c0284cc.language: Coherence describes the correlation between phases of waves or quantum states. Coherent systems maintain fixed phase relationships, enabling interference patterns. Decoherence occurs when environmental interactions destroy phase correlations.
c9f5cf94dd521a4d211c7a7dc353c7615c0284cc.script: coherence = abs(sum(cmath.exp(1j * phase) for phase in phases)) / len(phases)

459ef83110499d01fb63d480915d9ecbebbbeea4.name: Eigenvalue
459ef83110499d01fb63d480915d9ecbebbbeea4.language: An eigenvalue is a scalar λ such that a linear transformation A applied to eigenvector v yields a scalar multiple of v. Eigenvalues characterize the behavior of linear systems, appearing in quantum mechanics, vibration analysis, and principal component analysis.

b81cdb51691c2498ea7155d5f34f99b125e8e5e6.name: Convolution
b81cdb51691c2498ea7155d5f34f99b125e8e5e6.language: Convolution is a mathematical operation combining two functions to produce a third, expressing how one function modifies the other. It appears in signal processing, probability theory, and neural networks. The convolution theorem relates convolution to multiplication in frequency domain.

c82e0cfa4d0d4ea565e6c49efd7ef13b9ba72897.name: Bijection
c82e0cfa4d0d4ea565e6c49efd7ef13b9ba72897.math: f: A → B | one-to-one and onto
c82e0cfa4d0d4ea565e6c49efd7ef13b9ba72897.language: A bijection is a function that is both injective (one-to-one) and surjective (onto), establishing a perfect pairing between elements of two sets. Bijections prove sets have equal cardinality and enable invertible mappings.
c82e0cfa4d0d4ea565e6c49efd7ef13b9ba72897.script: is_bijection = len(set(f(x) for x in domain)) == len(domain) == len(codomain)

e5541301a033c70f5325812a38bfe0622603b2d9.name: Idempotent
e5541301a033c70f5325812a38bfe0622603b2d9.language: An idempotent operation produces the same result when applied multiple times as when applied once. Examples include absolute value, set union with itself, and database UPSERT operations. Idempotency ensures system stability under repeated operations.
e5541301a033c70f5325812a38bfe0622603b2d9.script: is_idempotent = all(f(f(x)) == f(x) for x in test_values)

4020e85f78d5c0ea0c37626b2d7ca8b9997fb4a8.name: Homeomorphism
4020e85f78d5c0ea0c37626b2d7ca8b9997fb4a8.math: f: X → Y | continuous bijection with continuous inverse
4020e85f78d5c0ea0c37626b2d7ca8b9997fb4a8.language: A homeomorphism is a continuous bijection with a continuous inverse, preserving topological properties. Homeomorphic spaces are topologically equivalent - a coffee cup is homeomorphic to a donut. Homeomorphisms classify spaces by their invariant properties.
4020e85f78d5c0ea0c37626b2d7ca8b9997fb4a8.script: is_homeomorphism = is_continuous(f) and is_bijection(f) and is_continuous(inverse(f))

0c3193ff2dbe86633e9890ac887500e92161f486.name: Isomorphism
0c3193ff2dbe86633e9890ac887500e92161f486.language: An isomorphism is a bijective mapping that preserves structure between algebraic objects. Isomorphic structures are mathematically identical in their abstract properties. Group isomorphisms preserve group operations; ring isomorphisms preserve both addition and multiplication.
0c3193ff2dbe86633e9890ac887500e92161f486.script: is_isomorphism = is_bijection(phi) and preserves_operation(phi, op1, op2)

f7dbae58d02b163fe5f6b7834145cf859c21c3a0.name: Gradient
f7dbae58d02b163fe5f6b7834145cf859c21c3a0.language: The gradient is a vector of partial derivatives pointing in the direction of steepest ascent. Its magnitude indicates the rate of change. Gradient descent uses the negative gradient to find function minima, fundamental to machine learning optimization.
f7dbae58d02b163fe5f6b7834145cf859c21c3a0.script: gradient = numpy.array([partial_derivative(f, x, i) for i in range(len(x))])

35c4089f5be78ef7b2bc45d1964b3ce313f11166.name: Divergence
35c4089f5be78ef7b2bc45d1964b3ce313f11166.language: Divergence measures the rate at which a vector field spreads out from a point. Positive divergence indicates a source; negative indicates a sink. Maxwell's equations use divergence to relate electric field to charge density.
35c4089f5be78ef7b2bc45d1964b3ce313f11166.script: divergence = sum(partial_derivative(F[i], x, i) for i in range(3))

862612ef5f36b7925da7b4e07fd37deee0297f9e.name: Curl
862612ef5f36b7925da7b4e07fd37deee0297f9e.language: Curl measures the rotation or circulation of a vector field around a point. A non-zero curl indicates rotational flow. In electromagnetism, the curl of the electric field relates to changing magnetic flux.

da8c02608aec34a24d9a114682f4650a02448b3f.name: Manifold
da8c02608aec34a24d9a114682f4650a02448b3f.language: A manifold is a topological space that locally resembles Euclidean space. The Earth's surface is a 2-manifold embedded in 3D space. General relativity models spacetime as a 4-dimensional pseudo-Riemannian manifold.
da8c02608aec34a24d9a114682f4650a02448b3f.script: is_manifold = all(neighborhood_homeomorphic_to_Rn(p) for p in space)

1e1369ab90a82078f7912b603c527327005b8508.name: Tensor
1e1369ab90a82078f7912b603c527327005b8508.math: T: V^p × V*^q → ℝ | Multilinear map
1e1369ab90a82078f7912b603c527327005b8508.language: A tensor is a multilinear map generalizing scalars, vectors, and matrices to higher dimensions. Tensors transform according to specific rules under coordinate changes. They describe physical quantities like stress, electromagnetic fields, and spacetime curvature.

620fb19f2a8018c2c186cf6f0bfc0e58c5a5bc2e.name: Topology
620fb19f2a8018c2c186cf6f0bfc0e58c5a5bc2e.language: Topology studies properties preserved under continuous deformations. A topology on a set defines which subsets are 'open'. Topological invariants like genus and homotopy groups classify spaces. Topology underlies concepts of continuity, connectedness, and compactness.
620fb19f2a8018c2c186cf6f0bfc0e58c5a5bc2e.script: is_topology = contains_empty_and_full(tau) and closed_under_union(tau) and closed_under_finite_intersection(tau)

d70f8dcd0254f8d85c399f9cad7462a15d07fe10.name: Homotopy
d70f8dcd0254f8d85c399f9cad7462a15d07fe10.language: A homotopy is a continuous deformation between two continuous functions. Homotopic paths can be continuously transformed into each other. Homotopy groups classify topological spaces by their 'holes' at different dimensions.

e9f8d604c083ae0da33d2b6b1f4517b7fbe837ba.name: Ergodic
e9f8d604c083ae0da33d2b6b1f4517b7fbe837ba.language: An ergodic system has the property that time averages equal ensemble averages. Over long times, the system visits all accessible states proportionally. Ergodicity is fundamental to statistical mechanics and enables inference from single trajectories.

265faf4673ff6873269bbb2c42f34edd6b4ee4f4.name: Stochastic
265faf4673ff6873269bbb2c42f34edd6b4ee4f4.language: A stochastic process is a collection of random variables indexed by time or space. Unlike deterministic systems, stochastic processes incorporate randomness. Examples include Brownian motion, Markov chains, and stock price models.

0457217d98d824c45aead323f979765d419ba00d.name: Orthogonal
0457217d98d824c45aead323f979765d419ba00d.language: Orthogonal vectors have zero inner product, meaning they are perpendicular in the geometric sense. Orthogonal bases simplify computations and decompositions. Orthogonal matrices preserve lengths and angles under transformation.

5cf850f3fe4da5a3d195d30c4198f0ecdb8d18c0.name: Hermitian
5cf850f3fe4da5a3d195d30c4198f0ecdb8d18c0.language: A Hermitian matrix equals its conjugate transpose. Hermitian matrices have real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors. In quantum mechanics, observables are represented by Hermitian operators, ensuring real measurement outcomes.

89533127b9c58cc9cdd488338fab3c61869a1b05.name: Unitary
89533127b9c58cc9cdd488338fab3c61869a1b05.language: A unitary matrix preserves inner products and norms. Unitary transformations represent reversible quantum operations. The set of unitary matrices forms a Lie group, fundamental to quantum computing and particle physics.

17a8406dbc80fd69d5bf18ae34c8c0488fc39d8f.name: Commutator
17a8406dbc80fd69d5bf18ae34c8c0488fc39d8f.language: The commutator measures how much two operators fail to commute. Zero commutator means the operators can be simultaneously diagonalized. In quantum mechanics, non-zero commutators lead to uncertainty relations.

3d39a8c19b1c7a59a9d61cdc87c3596a9d1ab23f.name: Determinant
3d39a8c19b1c7a59a9d61cdc87c3596a9d1ab23f.language: The determinant is a scalar value encoding properties of a square matrix. It equals the signed volume of the parallelepiped spanned by column vectors. Zero determinant indicates singular matrix; non-zero allows inversion.

51b3c3d154bd54a94bc3fc5749b6ad3d252b9880.name: Trace
51b3c3d154bd54a94bc3fc5749b6ad3d252b9880.language: The trace is the sum of diagonal elements of a square matrix. It equals the sum of eigenvalues and is invariant under similarity transformations. Trace appears in quantum mechanics as expectation values.

f6f02cd597f1f52316ec7eeb7e89d3f4c7221fa4.name: Norm
f6f02cd597f1f52316ec7eeb7e89d3f4c7221fa4.language: A norm measures the size or length of a vector. The Euclidean norm (L2) gives geometric distance. Other norms (L1, L∞, Frobenius) have different properties useful in optimization and analysis.

cfdc84cff81eadeb42cba2989aa5671165bedd68.name: Metric
cfdc84cff81eadeb42cba2989aa5671165bedd68.language: A metric is a function defining distance between points satisfying positivity, symmetry, and triangle inequality. Metrics enable concepts of convergence, continuity, and completeness. Different metrics capture different notions of similarity.
cfdc84cff81eadeb42cba2989aa5671165bedd68.script: metric = lambda x, y: numpy.sqrt(sum((a-b)**2 for a, b in zip(x, y)))

65173c79ae6a7935a1fc6df57554ad13a52e9fdc.name: Kernel
65173c79ae6a7935a1fc6df57554ad13a52e9fdc.language: The kernel of a linear map is the set of vectors mapped to zero. Kernel dimension (nullity) relates to rank via rank-nullity theorem. In machine learning, kernel functions enable nonlinear transformations.
65173c79ae6a7935a1fc6df57554ad13a52e9fdc.script: kernel = [v for v in basis if numpy.allclose(f(v), 0)]

f0246c552a559319e10ecd83503ed61dc30df3c1.name: Spectrum
f0246c552a559319e10ecd83503ed61dc30df3c1.language: The spectrum of an operator is the set of its eigenvalues. Spectral analysis decomposes operators into simpler components. Spectral theory connects linear algebra, functional analysis, and quantum mechanics.

dc25c082185234d1a1de812ece386e6bc4729382.name: Invariant
dc25c082185234d1a1de812ece386e6bc4729382.language: An invariant is a quantity unchanged by a transformation or symmetry operation. Conservation laws arise from symmetry invariants. Topological invariants classify spaces; algebraic invariants classify structures.
dc25c082185234d1a1de812ece386e6bc4729382.script: is_invariant = all(f(T(x)) == f(x) for x in domain for T in transformations)

f1e02477efb00bb422bff09444cd1fc53a0ee376.name: Python List
f1e02477efb00bb422bff09444cd1fc53a0ee376.language: A Python list is a mutable, ordered sequence of elements. Lists support indexing, slicing, and dynamic resizing. They can contain mixed types and nested structures. Common operations include append, extend, insert, remove, and sort.

80c13e076e5d6613ccee45098d86b545cf6a3f7b.name: Python Dict
80c13e076e5d6613ccee45098d86b545cf6a3f7b.language: A Python dictionary is a mutable mapping of keys to values with O(1) average lookup. Keys must be hashable; values can be any type. Dictionaries maintain insertion order since Python 3.7. Methods include get, keys, values, items, update.

f260f032dedeb078de478fa4097a1f9f1d2d5222.name: Python Set
f260f032dedeb078de478fa4097a1f9f1d2d5222.language: A Python set is an unordered collection of unique hashable elements. Sets support mathematical operations: union, intersection, difference, symmetric difference. Membership testing is O(1). Frozensets are immutable variants.

6122cfcee0be35879836a9e231c8a5e627d4a1dc.name: Python Tuple
6122cfcee0be35879836a9e231c8a5e627d4a1dc.language: A Python tuple is an immutable, ordered sequence. Tuples are hashable if all elements are hashable, enabling use as dictionary keys. Named tuples provide field access by name. Tuple unpacking enables multiple assignment.
6122cfcee0be35879836a9e231c8a5e627d4a1dc.script: my_tuple = (1, 2, 3); a, b, c = my_tuple; Point = namedtuple('Point', ['x', 'y'])

67eb61321c6d1bccd001aae73d10ee83609c10f5.name: Python Comprehension
67eb61321c6d1bccd001aae73d10ee83609c10f5.math: [expr for x in iterable if condition]
67eb61321c6d1bccd001aae73d10ee83609c10f5.language: List comprehensions provide concise syntax for creating lists from iterables. They combine mapping and filtering in a single expression. Dict and set comprehensions use similar syntax. Generator expressions use parentheses for lazy evaluation.
67eb61321c6d1bccd001aae73d10ee83609c10f5.script: squares = [x**2 for x in range(10)]; evens = [x for x in range(20) if x % 2 == 0]

eebf1ff6cb79a137cbb2c93845ee85e683caa6fd.name: Python Generator
eebf1ff6cb79a137cbb2c93845ee85e683caa6fd.language: A generator is a function that yields values lazily, maintaining state between calls. Generators are memory-efficient for large sequences. Generator expressions create anonymous generators. The send() method enables bidirectional communication.
eebf1ff6cb79a137cbb2c93845ee85e683caa6fd.script: def fibonacci(): a, b = 0, 1; while True: yield a; a, b = b, a + b

b433bc7f597884724bdde40a1a21e652113e1525.name: Python Decorator
b433bc7f597884724bdde40a1a21e652113e1525.language: A decorator is a function that modifies another function's behavior. Decorators use the @ syntax for clean application. Common uses include logging, timing, caching, and access control. functools.wraps preserves decorated function metadata.

577d84cfb246df40f395c26c8b3291018540cc0f.name: Python Lambda
577d84cfb246df40f395c26c8b3291018540cc0f.language: Lambda creates small anonymous functions in a single expression. Lambdas are useful for short callbacks and key functions. They can access enclosing scope variables. Complex logic should use regular def statements.
577d84cfb246df40f395c26c8b3291018540cc0f.script: square = lambda x: x**2; sorted_data = sorted(items, key=lambda x: x['value'])

6b38300b32edb1959d2acdc8b31c0af9dde3c3bf.name: Python Map
6b38300b32edb1959d2acdc8b31c0af9dde3c3bf.language: Map applies a function to each element of an iterable, returning an iterator. It enables functional-style transformations. Multiple iterables can be mapped in parallel. For complex operations, list comprehensions may be clearer.
6b38300b32edb1959d2acdc8b31c0af9dde3c3bf.script: doubled = list(map(lambda x: x * 2, [1, 2, 3, 4])); pairs = list(map(lambda a, b: a + b, [1, 2], [3, 4]))

a84a86b9975f25cba17e10507d8e410ffb83ee4e.name: Python Filter
a84a86b9975f25cba17e10507d8e410ffb83ee4e.language: Filter returns an iterator of elements for which the predicate returns True. It enables functional-style selection. None as predicate filters falsy values. List comprehensions with if clauses provide similar functionality.
a84a86b9975f25cba17e10507d8e410ffb83ee4e.script: positives = list(filter(lambda x: x > 0, [-1, 0, 1, 2])); truthy = list(filter(None, [0, 1, '', 'a']))

fe2721bbaffba34ab20d770bc01f994af72d73d5.name: Python Reduce
fe2721bbaffba34ab20d770bc01f994af72d73d5.language: Reduce applies a binary function cumulatively to iterable elements, reducing to a single value. It's in functools module. Common reductions: sum, product, max, min. Explicit loops may be clearer for complex reductions.
fe2721bbaffba34ab20d770bc01f994af72d73d5.script: from functools import reduce; product = reduce(lambda a, b: a * b, [1, 2, 3, 4], 1)

b7bb5ba92cf322f595569b79a14d95a255d55e77.name: Python Zip
b7bb5ba92cf322f595569b79a14d95a255d55e77.language: Zip combines multiple iterables element-wise into tuples. It stops at the shortest iterable; itertools.zip_longest pads shorter ones. Zip is useful for parallel iteration and transposing data structures.

76ac5eadfe5a8c4e690b3d0894033086c7262536.name: Python Enumerate
76ac5eadfe5a8c4e690b3d0894033086c7262536.language: Enumerate adds a counter to an iterable, yielding (index, value) pairs. The start parameter sets the initial index. It's cleaner than manual index tracking. Useful for indexed iteration and creating numbered lists.
76ac5eadfe5a8c4e690b3d0894033086c7262536.script: for i, item in enumerate(['a', 'b', 'c'], start=1): print(f'{i}: {item}')

5cf939a1959662922848389e1a0d01fb8625ca66.name: Python Sorted
5cf939a1959662922848389e1a0d01fb8625ca66.language: Sorted returns a new sorted list from any iterable. The key function extracts comparison values. Reverse=True sorts descending. For in-place sorting of lists, use list.sort(). Sorting is stable (preserves order of equal elements).
5cf939a1959662922848389e1a0d01fb8625ca66.script: sorted_nums = sorted([3, 1, 4, 1, 5]); by_length = sorted(words, key=len, reverse=True)

650df889c5bd5e58f4aa267b17b935a82d3845d2.name: Python Class
650df889c5bd5e58f4aa267b17b935a82d3845d2.language: A class defines a blueprint for creating objects with attributes and methods. Classes support inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism. Special methods (__init__, __str__, etc.) customize behavior. Dataclasses reduce boilerplate.

1057dad480b8ad7b311480f0f130372ff3a8b6a5.name: Python Exception
1057dad480b8ad7b311480f0f130372ff3a8b6a5.language: Exception handling separates error handling from normal flow. Try blocks contain risky code; except blocks handle specific exceptions. Finally always executes for cleanup. Raise creates exceptions; custom exceptions extend Exception.

ccfe73e8be975f43a716911eb49eecaf5efe2c41.name: Python Context_Manager
ccfe73e8be975f43a716911eb49eecaf5efe2c41.math: with resource as r: | Automatic cleanup
ccfe73e8be975f43a716911eb49eecaf5efe2c41.language: Context managers ensure proper resource acquisition and release. The with statement calls __enter__ and __exit__ methods. contextlib provides utilities for creating context managers. Common uses: files, locks, database connections.
ccfe73e8be975f43a716911eb49eecaf5efe2c41.script:
with open('file.txt', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()  # File automatically closed

dae4a55a1b5f3da4a132e434f62bd070739a13d8.name: Python Iterator
dae4a55a1b5f3da4a132e434f62bd070739a13d8.language: An iterator is an object implementing __iter__ and __next__ methods. Iterators maintain state and produce values on demand. StopIteration signals exhaustion. Itertools provides powerful iterator combinators.
dae4a55a1b5f3da4a132e434f62bd070739a13d8.script:
class Counter:
    def __init__(self, n): self.n = n; self.i = 0
    def __iter__(self): return self
    def __next__(self): if self.i >= self.n: raise StopIteration; self.i += 1; return self.i

3297ef1a62900d0ec32cfe524e33b416b01ef66a.name: Python Async
3297ef1a62900d0ec32cfe524e33b416b01ef66a.math: async def f(): await ... | Concurrent I/O
3297ef1a62900d0ec32cfe524e33b416b01ef66a.language: Async functions enable concurrent I/O operations without threads. Await suspends execution until a coroutine completes. asyncio provides the event loop and utilities. Async is ideal for I/O-bound tasks like network requests.
3297ef1a62900d0ec32cfe524e33b416b01ef66a.script:
async def fetch(url):
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.get(url) as response:
            return await response.text()

b9938450077b5628ffa44e0a07db5c24a0e916e0.name: Python Dataclass
b9938450077b5628ffa44e0a07db5c24a0e916e0.language: Dataclasses automatically generate __init__, __repr__, __eq__, and other methods. They reduce boilerplate for data-holding classes. Field() customizes individual fields. frozen=True makes instances immutable and hashable.

20b991c37d1278043d5253ca08cbdb0206b79bc4.name: Physics: Newton1
20b991c37d1278043d5253ca08cbdb0206b79bc4.language: Newton's First Law (Inertia): An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in uniform motion, unless acted upon by a net external force. This defines inertial reference frames and establishes that force causes acceleration, not velocity.

528ca6cb84b56cc56c2a320f9aa487c74268417d.name: Physics: Newton2
528ca6cb84b56cc56c2a320f9aa487c74268417d.math: F = ma | Force equals mass times acceleration
528ca6cb84b56cc56c2a320f9aa487c74268417d.language: Newton's Second Law: The net force on an object equals its mass times acceleration. This is the fundamental equation of classical mechanics, relating force, mass, and motion. It applies in inertial frames and generalizes to F = dp/dt.
528ca6cb84b56cc56c2a320f9aa487c74268417d.script: force = mass * acceleration; acceleration = force / mass

5dacd02693977a2ce1ce039799b09e58a9f9f20b.name: Physics: Newton3
5dacd02693977a2ce1ce039799b09e58a9f9f20b.language: Newton's Third Law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. Forces always occur in pairs acting on different objects. This law enables analysis of collisions, propulsion, and structural forces.

dfa0cd717de36699becad880d2df1ca3d3871c93.name: Physics: Conservation Energy
dfa0cd717de36699becad880d2df1ca3d3871c93.math: E_total = constant | Energy neither created nor destroyed
dfa0cd717de36699becad880d2df1ca3d3871c93.language: Conservation of Energy: In an isolated system, total energy remains constant. Energy transforms between kinetic, potential, thermal, and other forms. This law underlies thermodynamics and is connected to time-translation symmetry.
dfa0cd717de36699becad880d2df1ca3d3871c93.script: E_initial = E_final; KE + PE + thermal + other = constant

1aa6eb8969d8eb5efb73450fa0d5d46a40765a02.name: Physics: Conservation Momentum
1aa6eb8969d8eb5efb73450fa0d5d46a40765a02.language: Conservation of Momentum: In an isolated system, total momentum remains constant. This governs collisions, explosions, and rocket propulsion. Connected to space-translation symmetry via Noether's theorem.
1aa6eb8969d8eb5efb73450fa0d5d46a40765a02.script: p_initial = p_final; m1*v1_i + m2*v2_i = m1*v1_f + m2*v2_f

dc79f9e951cd2501da0f25d3896aaeb63acef374.name: Physics: Thermodynamics1
dc79f9e951cd2501da0f25d3896aaeb63acef374.math: ΔU = Q - W | Internal energy change
dc79f9e951cd2501da0f25d3896aaeb63acef374.language: First Law of Thermodynamics: The change in internal energy equals heat added minus work done by the system. This is conservation of energy applied to thermodynamic systems. It defines the relationship between heat, work, and energy.

82dd654505fc9e65f8378a5388fea64532c38283.name: Physics: Thermodynamics2
82dd654505fc9e65f8378a5388fea64532c38283.language: Second Law of Thermodynamics: In an isolated system, entropy never decreases. Heat flows from hot to cold spontaneously. This establishes the arrow of time and limits the efficiency of heat engines.

edca2cb15c44d52f98046080befbb0b5d5e7dc35.name: Physics: Maxwell Gauss E
edca2cb15c44d52f98046080befbb0b5d5e7dc35.language: Gauss's Law for Electricity: The divergence of the electric field equals charge density divided by permittivity. Electric field lines originate from positive charges and terminate on negative charges. Integral form relates flux to enclosed charge.

cac12cb82f3b0261a705cef1aa97a0745f69cb0c.name: Physics: Maxwell Gauss B
cac12cb82f3b0261a705cef1aa97a0745f69cb0c.language: Gauss's Law for Magnetism: The divergence of the magnetic field is zero. Magnetic field lines form closed loops; there are no magnetic monopoles. This constrains the topology of magnetic fields.

dba3e866daafd4a816cab1de4d2595e2ca71c509.name: Physics: Maxwell Faraday
dba3e866daafd4a816cab1de4d2595e2ca71c509.language: Faraday's Law of Induction: A changing magnetic field induces an electric field. This is the principle behind generators, transformers, and electromagnetic waves. The negative sign reflects Lenz's law.

4e5b3aee1024f32b7cb812adff96d8b15cf47c94.name: Physics: Maxwell Ampere
4e5b3aee1024f32b7cb812adff96d8b15cf47c94.language: Ampère-Maxwell Law: Magnetic field curl equals current density plus displacement current. Maxwell's addition of displacement current enabled electromagnetic wave prediction. This completes the symmetry of Maxwell's equations.
4e5b3aee1024f32b7cb812adff96d8b15cf47c94.script: curl_B = mu_0 * J + mu_0 * epsilon_0 * dE_dt

6834f2a0eb87aec79af06533d5dcbc73e41f123f.name: Physics: Schrodinger
6834f2a0eb87aec79af06533d5dcbc73e41f123f.language: Schrödinger Equation: Describes quantum state evolution over time. The Hamiltonian operator Ĥ determines dynamics. Solutions are wavefunctions whose squared magnitude gives probability density. This is the foundation of quantum mechanics.
6834f2a0eb87aec79af06533d5dcbc73e41f123f.script: psi_t = evolve(H, psi_0, t); probability = abs(psi)**2

3e36ea483a059e0457e54e40180d0f77681b8025.name: Physics: Heisenberg
3e36ea483a059e0457e54e40180d0f77681b8025.language: Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle: Position and momentum cannot be simultaneously known with arbitrary precision. This is fundamental, not a measurement limitation. Similar relations hold for energy-time and other conjugate pairs.

14d992349e924ab4622edaac3dee05368dd0eba9.name: Physics: Special Relativity
14d992349e924ab4622edaac3dee05368dd0eba9.language: Einstein's Mass-Energy Equivalence: Mass and energy are interconvertible. A small mass contains enormous energy (c² ≈ 9×10¹⁶ m²/s²). This underlies nuclear reactions and particle physics. Full relation: E² = (pc)² + (mc²)².

313702fb3f1cf2caf64817b3dbfdcfb89fdb20af.name: Physics: Lorentz
313702fb3f1cf2caf64817b3dbfdcfb89fdb20af.language: Lorentz Factor: Quantifies relativistic effects as velocity approaches light speed. Time dilates, length contracts, and mass increases by factor γ. At v=0, γ=1; as v→c, γ→∞. This transforms between inertial frames.

31bb6e19c39824ff1d229e31a94841af2bb69956.name: Physics: Planck
31bb6e19c39824ff1d229e31a94841af2bb69956.language: Planck's Relation: Energy of a photon equals Planck's constant times frequency. This introduced quantization to physics, resolving the ultraviolet catastrophe. It connects wave (frequency) and particle (energy) descriptions of light.

d586bff057c132965a0f6481c7b040f3dce58643.name: Physics: Coulomb
d586bff057c132965a0f6481c7b040f3dce58643.language: Coulomb's Law: The electrostatic force between charges is proportional to their product and inversely proportional to distance squared. Like charges repel; opposite charges attract. This parallels gravitational force structure.

aa13f4ad18cfc674211377db6ccc49dc040132a3.name: Physics: Gravity
aa13f4ad18cfc674211377db6ccc49dc040132a3.language: Newton's Law of Gravitation: Every mass attracts every other mass with force proportional to their product and inversely proportional to distance squared. G is the gravitational constant. This describes planetary motion and tides.

c19f070079d69c4a614effa45dd748da6554f89b.name: Physics: Ideal Gas
c19f070079d69c4a614effa45dd748da6554f89b.language: Ideal Gas Law: Relates pressure, volume, amount, and temperature of an ideal gas. R is the universal gas constant. Real gases deviate at high pressure or low temperature. This combines Boyle's, Charles's, and Avogadro's laws.

5776a3c954b4d0c587ed84c5857add65002ddbe7.name: Physics: Wave
5776a3c954b4d0c587ed84c5857add65002ddbe7.language: Wave Equation: Wave velocity equals frequency times wavelength. This applies to all waves: mechanical, electromagnetic, matter waves. Higher frequency means shorter wavelength at constant velocity. Dispersion occurs when v depends on f.
5776a3c954b4d0c587ed84c5857add65002ddbe7.script: velocity = frequency * wavelength; wavelength = velocity / frequency

dc2cfd2765b37343ce675984ad2f14d4a098d7d0.name: Constant: Pi
dc2cfd2765b37343ce675984ad2f14d4a098d7d0.language: Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter. It is irrational and transcendental, appearing throughout mathematics and physics. Pi relates to periodicity, waves, and circular motion. Computed to trillions of digits.
dc2cfd2765b37343ce675984ad2f14d4a098d7d0.script: import math; pi = math.pi; circumference = 2 * pi * radius

eb94f9fdc1d36eecd6727eeb88627c95c051dd3f.name: Constant: E
eb94f9fdc1d36eecd6727eeb88627c95c051dd3f.language: Euler's number e is the base of natural logarithms. It is the unique number where d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ. e appears in compound interest, probability, and differential equations. e = lim(1 + 1/n)ⁿ as n→∞.
eb94f9fdc1d36eecd6727eeb88627c95c051dd3f.script: import math; e = math.e; natural_exp = math.exp(x)

3805e63f5c13b8afb99806ac36df8c702a5d0061.name: Constant: Phi
3805e63f5c13b8afb99806ac36df8c702a5d0061.language: The golden ratio φ appears when a line is divided so the whole is to the larger part as the larger is to the smaller. It appears in Fibonacci sequences, art, architecture, and phyllotaxis. φ² = φ + 1.

b14c3b32ebae706591786d6022ad01feb455cb19.name: Constant: Sqrt2
b14c3b32ebae706591786d6022ad01feb455cb19.language: The square root of 2 is the first proven irrational number (by the Pythagoreans). It is the diagonal of a unit square and the ratio of frequencies in equal temperament music. √2 = 2^(1/2).

2348d25a6deb26b2fa2b5980182b0bd329068d91.name: Constant: Euler Gamma
2348d25a6deb26b2fa2b5980182b0bd329068d91.language: The Euler-Mascheroni constant γ is the limiting difference between the harmonic series and natural logarithm. It appears in number theory, analysis, and the gamma function. Its rationality is unknown.

38256d9f8909d62c4265f6b65949e8484560dceb.name: Constant: Fine Structure
38256d9f8909d62c4265f6b65949e8484560dceb.language: The fine-structure constant α characterizes electromagnetic interaction strength. It is dimensionless, combining e, ℏ, c, and ε₀. α ≈ 1/137 determines atomic spectra and QED corrections. Its value is unexplained.

8b2ba51386f23b13a9c9573c142fc92e4256fc0f.name: Constant: Avogadro
8b2ba51386f23b13a9c9573c142fc92e4256fc0f.language: Avogadro's number is the number of entities in one mole. It connects atomic and macroscopic scales. One mole of carbon-12 has mass exactly 12 grams. Nₐ defines the mole in the SI system.

bda92eaee442f20045fcad8e6222fc43eeb1ae30.name: Constant: Planck Const
bda92eaee442f20045fcad8e6222fc43eeb1ae30.language: Planck's constant h is the quantum of action. It sets the scale of quantum effects. ℏ = h/2π appears in the uncertainty principle and Schrödinger equation. h defines the kilogram in the SI system.

01694d9c6dd7c42b98b3e51f3957209dacd91feb.name: Constant: Speed Light
01694d9c6dd7c42b98b3e51f3957209dacd91feb.language: The speed of light in vacuum c is the universal speed limit. It is exact by definition in SI units. c connects space and time in relativity and appears in E=mc². Nothing with mass can reach c.

7fed9904233ebb875b2f7b37d58d6246255169ca.name: Constant: Gravitational
7fed9904233ebb875b2f7b37d58d6246255169ca.language: The gravitational constant G sets the strength of gravity. It is the least precisely known fundamental constant. G appears in Newton's law and Einstein's field equations. Measuring G is experimentally challenging.

a23941c0821b571dd194c35adb2c763b85bc0bec.name: Constant: Boltzmann
a23941c0821b571dd194c35adb2c763b85bc0bec.language: Boltzmann's constant k connects temperature to energy at the molecular level. It appears in the ideal gas law (R = Nₐk), entropy (S = k ln W), and thermal physics. k defines the kelvin in SI.

c82b533f38730fe2ab424f5fc6ad768292093eea.name: Constant: Electron Mass
c82b533f38730fe2ab424f5fc6ad768292093eea.language: The electron mass is a fundamental constant in atomic physics. Electrons are the lightest charged particles. The electron mass determines atomic structure, chemistry, and solid-state physics.

4a8abfb671d78806121657b8086986cfaba9c360.name: Constant: Proton Mass
4a8abfb671d78806121657b8086986cfaba9c360.language: The proton mass is about 1836 times the electron mass. Protons are composed of quarks and gluons. The proton mass determines nuclear physics and most visible matter mass.
